messages:
olga: Quick heads-up — we had a tenant that triggered ~1200 alerts in 10m this morning. Not a full outage, mostly latency tail spikes.
liam: ugh. Are those from a single route or many?
olga: Single route (embed-api) from one high-volume customer. It blew past the alert threshold because the SLO is strict and we have no per-tenant dampening.
maya: do we have telemetry to tell if these are true positives vs noisy back-pressure?
sam: telemetry shows elevated p99 and some retry storms. It looks like a client-side retry loop + some transient infra throttling.
liam: sounds like we should avoid global fanout on the console — we need per-tenant soft thresholds + quota-aware notify. Proposing API change: add notify.mode = ["immediate","quota-aware","suppress-preview"]
maya: +1 for quota-aware. Also want a preview UI so engs can simulate what would have fired before we flip it on. Otherwise we break on rollout.
olga: sketch of a minimal API patch:
```json
{
  "slo_id": "embed-api-latency",
  "window": "5m",
  "threshold_ms": 600,
  "notify": {
    "mode": "quota-aware",
    "burst_quota": 50,
    "sample_rate": 0.2
  }
}
```
liam: ok. A couple of constraints: (1) notify decisions must be deterministic for audit logs, (2) we need an efficient sampler in runtime (can't call console service per token).
sam: we can record the decision locally (per-tenant token) and emit a telemetry tag like notify_decision=quota_suppressed|notified. That makes the console show breakdowns later.
maya: UI preview idea: add a toggle on SLO edit to "Simulate on recent traffic" that will run the notify logic against the last 24h windows and show a heatmap of suppressed vs would-have-notified. No side effects.
olga: perf-wise, the simulate run can be a background job. We should limit to last 24h and paginate.
liam: API contract detail: new endpoint POST /slo/:id/simulate with body {window_start, window_end, mode_overrides}. Return is a list of buckets with counts. Keep it cheap (pre-aggregates).
maya: UX note — make it clear in the console that suppressed alerts still count against error budget, and only suppression affects notify fanout. Folks often assume suppression means 'ignored'.
sam: also suggestion: when suppression occurs due to quota, create a lightweight incident stub in the UI with an annotation "suppressed by quota: X of Y events" so customers can click through.
liam: we need to reconcile with rollouts — canary for notify.mode needs to be per-org rollout flag, not global. We don't want a half-rolled notify mode for multi-tenant clusters.
olga: agree. Per-org flagging + canary percentage. Deploy-bot: canary deploy for notify-sampler v2 scheduled at 03:00 UTC.
deploy-bot: :rocket: starting canary deploy notify-sampler v2 to 5% of orgs (deploy id: dpl-2025-4581). Monitoring hook: notify-sampler.error_count, sampling_discrepancy.
maya: operational checklist before flip: docs update, console copy explaining suppression, telemetry tag mapping, and sample-rate UI.
sam: one more: add a debug mode in logs so we can replay suppressed decisions — helpful when customers file support tickets claiming they weren't notified.
liam: small API tweak: return header X-SLO-SIM-ID when simulate runs so we can link logs/telemetry to simulation run.
olga: timeline proposal: spec PR today, runtime PR for sampler in 3 days, API + console PR in 1 week, canary after automated tests.
maya: sounds good. I'll draft the console mockups for simulate heatmap and suppressed-incident stub.
sam: I'll sketch telemetry fields and the pre-aggregate query shape.
liam: I'll own the API contract and rollout flags.
olga: thanks — will open a tracking ticket and a short RFC thread. Keep channel updated. :thumbsup:
